source_text: Μετέπειτα δὲ ἐπὶ τὸν ἡγεμόνα ἀχθέντων αὐτῶν κἀκείνου πάσῃ τῇ πρὸς ἡμᾶς ὠμότητι χρωμένου, Οὐέττιος Ἐπάγαθος, εἷς ἐκ τῶν ἀδελφῶν, πλήρωμα ἀγάπης τῆς πρὸς τὸν θεὸν καὶ πρὸς τὸν πλησίον κεχωρηκώς, οὗ καὶ ἐπὶ τοσοῦτον ἠκρίβωτο ἡ πολιτεία, ὡς καίπερ ὄντα νέον συνεξισοῦσθαι τῇ τοῦ πρεσβυτέρου Ζαχαρίου μαρτυρίᾳ· πεπόρευτο γοῦν ἐν πάσαις ταῖς ἐντολαῖς καὶ δικαιώμασι τοῦ κυρίου ἄμεμπτος καὶ πάσῃ τῇ πρὸς τὸν πλησίον λειτουργίᾳ ἄοκνος, ζῆλον θεοῦ πολὺν ἔχων καὶ ζέων τῷ πνεύματι· τοιοῦτος δή τις ὤν, τὴν οὕτως καθ᾽ ἡμῶν ἀλόγως γινομένην κρίσιν οὐκ ἐβάστασεν, ἀλλ᾽ ὑπερηγανάκτησε, καὶ ἠξίου καὶ αὐτὸς ἀκουσθῆναι ἀπολογούμενος ὑπὲρ τῶν ἀδελφῶν ὅτι μηδὲν ἄθεον μηδὲ ἀσεβὲς ἐστιν ἐν ἡμῖν. Τῶν δὲ περὶ τὸ βῆμα καταβοησάντων αὐτοῦ, καὶ γὰρ ἦν ἐπίσημος, καὶ τοῦ ἡγεμόνος μὴ ἀνασχομένου τῆς οὕτως ὑπ᾽ αὐτοῦ δικαίας προταθείσης ἀξιώσεως, ἀλλὰ μόνον τοῦτο πυθομένου εἰ καὶ αὐτὸς εἴη Χριστιανός, τοῦ δὲ λαμπροτάτῃ φωνῇ ὁμολογήσαντος, ἀνελήφθη καὶ αὐτὸς εἰς τὸν κλῆρον τῶν μαρτύρων, παράκλητος Χριστιανῶν χρηματίσας, ἔχων δὲ τὸν παράκλητον ἐν ἑαυτῷ, τὸ πνεῦμα τοῦ Ζαχαρίου, ὃ διὰ τοῦ πληρώματος τῆς ἀγάπης ἐνεδείξατο, εὐδοκήσας ὑπὲρ τῆς τῶν ἀδελφῶν ἀπολογίας καὶ τὴν ἑαυτοῦ ψυχήν· ἦν γὰρ καὶ ἔστιν γνήσιος Χριστοῦ μαθητής, ἀκολουθῶν τῷ ἀρνίῳ ὅπου ἂν ὑπάγῃ.
thought_title: A defender volunteers and is numbered with the martyrs
orientation: After being shut in prison until the governor arrives, the Christians are now led before him.
pass_a_gloss: But afterwards, when they were led before the governor and he employed all cruelty toward us, Vettius Epagathus, one from among the brothers and sisters in faith, having advanced to a fullness of love toward God and toward neighbor, whose manner of life also had been made exact to so great a degree that although being young he was held equal to the witness of the elder Zacharias; for he had walked blameless in all the commandments and ordinances of the Lord and untiring in all service toward neighbor, having much zeal for God and being fervent in spirit; being such a person, he did not bear the judgment so unreasonably taking place against us, but he was exceedingly indignant, and he asked that he himself also be heard speaking in defense of the brothers and sisters in faith, that nothing godless nor impious is among us. But those around the tribunal shouted against him, for he was prominent, and the governor did not endure the demand so justly proposed by him, but asked only this, whether he himself also was a Christian, and when he professed with clearest voice, he himself also was taken up into the lot of the martyrs, having become an advocate of Christians, but having the advocate in himself, the spirit of Zacharias, which he displayed through the fullness of love, having consented to give even his own life for the defense of the brothers and sisters in faith; for he was and is a genuine disciple of Christ, following the Lamb wherever it goes.

pass_b_english: When they were brought before the governor, and he turned all his cruelty against us, Vettius Epagathus stepped forward. He was one of the brothers and sisters in faith who had reached the full measure of love for God and for his neighbor, and his life was so exacting that, young as he was, he was ranked equal to the witness of the elder Zacharias. For he had lived blameless in all the commandments and decrees of the Lord (Luke 1:6), tireless in every service to his neighbor, with great zeal for God and fervent in spirit (Romans 12:11).

Being such a man, he could not bear so senseless a trial against us. He burned with anger and asked to be heard himself, pleading for the brothers and sisters in faith that there is nothing godless or impious among us. The people crowding the tribunal shouted him down, for he was a man of standing, and the governor would not accept the just request he had made. The governor asked him only this, whether he too was a Christian, and when Vettius professed the faith in a ringing voice, he too was taken up into the lot of the martyrs. He had stood as advocate for Christians, and he carried the advocate within himself, the spirit of Zacharias, which he showed through the fullness of his love, gladly offering even his own life for the defense of the brothers and sisters in faith. For he was and is a true disciple of Christ, following the Lamb wherever he goes (Revelation 14:4).
